pixelObservations: Single eye cross-section: anterior/corneal bulge to the left, roughly round globe, posterior wall and exiting optic-nerve bundle to the lower right. No panel letters.
The outer wall has multiple dark/white outlines; an inner dark lining follows the posterior globe and meets the nerve exit. Source hatching and irregular edge strokes are not measured microanatomy.
A transparent bulging anterior surface is in front of the iris and crystalline lens. The small anterior chamber lies between the cornea and iris.
The iris appears as dark upper/lower structures at the front of the lens. Its central gap is the pupil; callout 5 forks to the two edges of the aperture.
The lens is a convex transparent section immediately behind the pupil. The structure called muscle 7 is at the upper lens attachment; a corresponding lower attachment is visible.
The large clear internal chamber behind the lens is the vitreous. Callout 8 has a long upper-right oblique leader crossing the wall toward that chamber.
Callout 9 points to the inner posterior lining, not to the optic-nerve bundle. Callout 10 points to the bundle projecting to the lower right.
A horizontal dashed axis runs from the pupil/anterior region toward the posterior inner wall. It has no arrowheads and is not a ray, focal plane, or retinal-image arrow.
Labels 1 through 7 appear at the left in ascending vertical order from bottom to top; 8 is above the globe, 9 at upper right, 10 at right by the nerve.
No focal points, angle labels, object arrows, incident-ray arrowheads, grid, units, or numeric measurements occur in the figure itself.
Short tangential strokes above and below the globe are unnumbered surrounding anatomical/outline detail, not incoming optical rays.

pixelObservations: One shared optical frame, not two independently scaled panels. Eye outline is on the right, front facing left.
Two upright vertical object arrows stand on the same almost horizontal lower sight line: one at the far left, one around the middle. Their visible heights are approximately the same.
There are two upper oblique sight rays from the two object tips. Both travel rightward to the same eye vertex; the nearer-object ray is steeper.
The common lower ray/baseline runs from the far-object foot through the near-object foot toward and through the eye.
There are four incoming ray arrowheads: one on each upper ray, one on the far-to-near lower span and one on the near-to-eye lower span. Both vertical objects also have upward arrowheads.

The eye has a roughly circular posterior outline and a small left anterior bulge. The upper sight lines meet inside the anterior eye region, then continue across the interior below the lower sight line toward the back.
Two angle marks sit to the left of the eye between the lower ray and the respective upper sight ray. A smaller rightward mark has label phi_1; a larger leftward mark has label phi_2.
The phi_2 callout leader approaches the larger outer arc; phi_1 approaches the smaller inner arc. Both labels are beneath the lower sight line.
No named A/B/O/F points, distances, focal lengths, lens symbol, image-height arrow, units, grid, or numerical angle values are printed.
The rear-going line continuations show crossing direction, not a quantitatively calibrated multi-surface eye refraction construction.
relationships: Equal object heights, common baseline, nearer distance smaller than farther distance.
Both object-tip sight lines and the common lower line have one eye vertex.
Farther object subtends phi_1; nearer object subtends phi_2; phi_2 is greater than phi_1.
All four incident ray arrowheads point from the objects toward the eye.
Vertical objects remain upright; crossing of upper lines behind the vertex is retained.
Do not add a magnifier, spectacle correction, focal distance, angle value, or medical threshold to this figure.
